summary: In a wealthy restaurant filled with chamber music, Agent Smith and Cypher dine over a steak that Cypher knows is not real. Smith opens by asking, 'Do we have a deal, Mr. Reagan?' Cypher savors the illusory steak, declaring 'Ignorance is bliss,' and agrees to a deal on conditions: he does not want to remember anything, and wants to be rich and important, 'like an actor.' Smith promises, 'Whatever you want, Mr. Reagan.' Cypher then commits: Smith will get his body back into a power plant and reinsert him into the Matrix, and in return Cypher will deliver what Smith wants. When Smith names it — 'Access codes to the Zion mainframe' — Cypher says he does not know them but 'can give you the man who does,' whom Smith identifies as 'Morpheus.'

what_changes.before: A member of the Nebuchadnezzar crew who resents the real world and wishes he had taken the blue pill.
what_changes.after: He openly brokers a betrayal, offering to hand Morpheus over to the Machines in exchange for reinsertion into the Matrix as someone rich and important.
what_changes.evidence: All right. You get my body back in a power plant, reinsert me into the Matrix and I'll get you what you want.

what_changes.before: He is still negotiating terms and stating what he wants from the arrangement.
what_changes.after: The terms are accepted and the transaction is sealed by mutual agreement on the target.
what_changes.evidence: AGENT SMITH Whatever you want, Mr. Reagan. CYPHER All right.

what_changes.before: He seeks the access codes to the Zion mainframe, which would let the Machines strike Zion.
what_changes.after: He learns Cypher cannot give the codes but can deliver the man who has them, and names that man.
what_changes.evidence: CYPHER I told you I don't know them. But I can give you the man who does. AGENT SMITH Morpheus.

event_hint.one_line: Cypher strikes a deal with Agent Smith to betray Morpheus in exchange for being reinserted into the Matrix as a wealthy, important man.

minds.wants: To be put back into the Matrix, erased, and remade as someone rich and important — and to seal that exchange by handing over Morpheus.
minds.feels: A weary, almost relieved self-disgust he has rationalized into a philosophy. Nine years of grey food and cold has hollowed him out; he would rather be comfortably lied to than honestly free, and he is closing the door on the part of himself that once resisted.
minds.shows: Sensuous, smug relish — savoring the steak, smacking his lips, drinking wine like a man already living the good life. He performs contentment and casual greed as if this were just a business lunch.
minds.basis: He savors the steak while explaining he knows it isn't real ('Ignorance is bliss'), then immediately lists his terms — no memory, wealth, importance 'like an actor' — and commits to delivering 'the man who does' know the codes. The deliberate, loud eating is a performance aimed at the deal's payoff.

believes_about.belief: That Smith is a reliable business partner who will honor the terms and actually reinsert him.
believes_about.wrong_because: inferred: Smith is an Agent whose aim is Zion's destruction; the deal is expedient, and nothing in Smith's nature obligates him to keep a traitor comfortable once Morpheus is delivered.

believes_about.belief: That Smith needs him and therefore must be courted — hence the coyness of not naming Morpheus until Smith does.
believes_about.wrong_because: inferred: Smith already knows the target is Morpheus before Cypher says a word; the suspense is Cypher's small, self-protective theater, not real leverage.

minds.wants: The Zion mainframe access codes — and, failing the codes themselves, the man who holds them — obtained as cheaply and cleanly as possible.
minds.feels: Cold, patient certainty. He holds every advantage and can afford to let Cypher perform; beneath the politeness is contempt for a man so easily bought, which he masks as manners.
minds.shows: Formal, unhurried courtesy — 'Mr. Reagan,' 'Whatever you want.' He lets Cypher eat and talk, asking only the minimal confirming questions ('Then we have a deal?') and supplying the name 'Morpheus' as though merely finishing Cypher's thought.
minds.basis: He opens by pressing for closure ('Do we have a deal?'), grants every demand without haggling, and names Morpheus the instant Cypher offers 'the man who does,' showing he already knew the answer and only needed Cypher to say it.

believes_about.belief: That Cypher is a tool to be used and discarded, whose appetite makes him utterly predictable and controllable.
believes_about.wrong_because: inferred: Smith reads Cypher's greed as total weakness and does not register that a man willing to sell his whole crew is not loyal to anyone, including the Machines — a miscalculation the betrayal later depends on.

connects_back: sc-073: Cypher's 'Why didn't I take that blue pill?' toast and his bitterness about Morpheus's dead candidates are the emotional fuel that drives him to this table.
The 'actor' he wants to become is the inverse of the grey, cold reality of sc-071/073's ship — he is buying his way out of exactly that life.
sets_up: ev-023: Cypher's murder of Dozer and wounding of Tank — the physical enactment of the betrayal brokered here.
ev-023: The delivery of Morpheus into the Agents' hands, which is the 'man who does' know the codes.
ev-024: The crew's debate over Morpheus's fate and the rescue that follows, set in motion by this exchange.
dramatic_function: It converts private resentment into active treason, turning the film's emotional stakes from philosophical debate into a concrete countdown, and it binds the two antagonistic forces — a traitor and the Machines — in a transaction that will drive the coming catastrophe.
